articleTitle: The connection of one large power station to the main grid
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on CEGB/EDF/ENEL Collaboration on Power System Planning and Operation
abstract: The authors compare the methods used by EDF, ENEL and CEGB for the connection of one large power station to the main system. Two major issues are discussed: the principles of planning and site selection, and the connection of the new station to the main grid. For each utility the authors discuss the procedures used for siting, grid connection which includes power export considerations and security of supply to the auxiliaries. An example is given for each utility.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The use of linear flow estimation in computing codes for long term system planning
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on CEGB/EDF/ENEL Collaboration on Power System Planning and Operation
abstract: In the framework of CEGB, EDF and ENEL collaboration, the three utilities exchanged their point of view, practice and experience on models for long term planning studies, within working group 1/3 'Power system planning'. Two conclusions were drawn: linear flow estimation is still useful in such tools, and is the common core of three models developed by each utility-TRESCO, ORELIA and LODEN respectively; and the design of these models is dependent on the organization of the planning processes, on the predominant problems in each of them, and on the balance between tasks executed by the model and tasks left to the user. The authors discuss these two considerations, and underline four parameters important to the planner. These are: time horizon, geography, system analysis techniques, and uncertainty/variability. Each model is analysed along these four main lines, with an extra mathematical comment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Methodologies of reconstruction of system incidents
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on CEGB/EDF/ENEL Collaboration on Power System Planning and Operation
abstract: The reconstruction of real power system incidents has attained an important role in better understanding of power system behaviour with the final object of continually improving the quality and continuity of service. With this aim the 1/1 CEGB-EDE-ENEL Working Group created Task Force 1/4 in order to compare the points of view of the three utilities about the methodologies of reconstruction of system incidents. Apart from the necessary 'database for post-mortem analysis' (passive network parameters, reactances, time constants, types of regulators, and so on), a methodology of reconstruction of system incidents refers to the following three phases: the analysis of all the available experimental information and the reconstruction of the sequence of events; the simulation of the static and dynamic behaviour of the system during the various phases of the incident; and the definition of corrective measures. The authors discuss the first two points for each of the utilities and then briefly discuss corrective measures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparison of demand prediction practices in CEGB, EDF and ENEL
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on CEGB/EDF/ENEL Collaboration on Power System Planning and Operation
abstract: The author provides a comparison of practices in regard to demand prediction in the CEGB (England and Wales), EDF (France) and ENEL (Italy), all three utilities being responsible for the planning and operation of the public generation and transmission facilities in the respective countries. The author discusses: the systems, including reserve margins, interconnection, private generation, demand shaping and control; purpose, time spans and prediction frequency; demand prediction methodology; influence of weather conditions; and future developments. The information is presented in tabular form.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Discussion of voltage control schemes by CEGB, ENEL, and EDF
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on CEGB/EDF/ENEL Collaboration on Power System Planning and Operation
abstract: The authors present the functional requirements of the ENEL and EDF secondary voltage control systems, compare the technical solutions which have been brought into operation, and approach the question of the developments to come. They then present the CEGB point of view, which considers a centralized control system in conjunction with research in progress in the field of automatic generation control (AGC), and makes comparisons with ENEL and EDF viewpoints, concerning voltage control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
